newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds plod higher, spreads steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds plod higher, spreads steady.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities rose in slow trading on Friday, closely matching the performance of Treasuries, market experts said.

At 1500 EST/2000 GMT, mortgages were 2/32 to 5/32 firmer across the board, while comparable Treasuries were up 2/32 to 6/32. Analysts said activity slowed in both markets as investors' attention shifted to next week's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.
"We've seen very little today," one New York-based trader said. "Its been a very quiet day."
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was 4/32 higher at 100-15/32, yielding 107 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was up 3/32 at 100-08/32, while similar Freddie Mac issues were up 2/32 at 100-12/32.
The 10-year Treasury note was up 6/32 at 99-06/32 to yield 6.36 percent.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony will be heard by the Senate Banking Committee next Wednesday and by the House on Thursday.
